Bill.BriefDescription: Changing the mens rea required for committing the crime of assault of a child in the first degree from a recklessness standard to negligence standard when the result is great bodily harm.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to first degree assault of a child; and amendingRCW 9A.36.120.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 9A.36.120 and 1992 c 145 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A person eighteen years of age or older is guilty of the crimeof assault of a child in the first degree if the child is under the ageof thirteen and the person: (a) Commits the crime of assault in the first degree, as defined inRCW 9A.36.011, against the child; or (b) Intentionally assaults the child and either: (i) ((Recklessly)) Negligently inflicts great bodily harm; or (ii) Causes substantial bodily harm, and the person has previouslyengaged in a pattern or practice either of (A) assaulting the childwhich has resulted in bodily harm that is greater than transientphysical pain or minor temporary marks, or (B) causing the childphysical pain or agony that is equivalent to that produced by torture. p. 1 HB 2723 (2) Assault of a child in the first degree is a class A felony.
